gameVerifiedNote: Not run in the game. Every signature, field offset and RVA below is read from the current build's own interop wrappers and dump; the behaviour of the five rows is exercised by ForgeMap/tests/InteractionFacts against game doubles, so what is proven here is the shape of the native surface, not its timing in a running level.
readback: Interact_Base and Interact_Timed as the interop assembly exposes them: every member below is a public member of the generated wrapper, so a Harmony postfix on the game method it wraps can read it without reflection. The wrappers live in Modules-ASM.dll and were decompiled from the QA profile's interop folder; the dump rows are from dump.cs of the same build.

hooks.name: PlayerSetSelected
hooks.readback: The selection bit the interactor sets when the player aims at an interactable, and the interactor's own answer to `PlayerCanInteract` for that player. The postfix reads `IsSelected` and the answer and reports `requested` when the selection went up and the answer is yes, `failed` when it is no.
hooks.evidence: Interact_Base.cs (interop wrapper) lines 437-448; dump.cs 563490-563492 (interop-visible) and the same class body's own slot table

hooks.name: Update
hooks.readback: The shared interaction timer once per frame: `m_timerIsActive` is the window that `started` reports on its rising edge and that closing below the top of its range reports as `cancelled`, `m_timerProgressRel` is the 0-to-1 fraction the progress bands are read from, and `m_interactTargetAgent` is the player the interaction belongs to.

hooks.name: Update
hooks.readback: The same per-frame readback for an interactable that carries no timer at all — `Interact_SimpleButton`, `Interact_SimpleDoorButton`, `Interact_Generic`, `Interact_Terminal`, `Interact_Elevator` and the other `Interact_Base` subclasses. Its request is the whole interaction, so `requested` and `started` are published for one selection and the refusal answer reports `failed`.
hooks.evidence: Interact_Base.cs (interop wrapper) lines 525-534; Interact_SimpleButton.cs 100-128 and Interact_Generic.cs (no timer member); dump.cs 564184-564198

hooks.name: SetActive
hooks.readback: The interactable leaving the world. Its interaction window is dropped with it, so a request that never started cannot be reported again by an interactable that is gone.

facts.native: Interact_Base.IsSelected rising while the interactor's answer is yes. The fact reports the entity the interactable resolves to through the map-object lookup, the acting player when the player half answers for the agent, and the fixed `requested` phase.
Interact_Timed.m_timerIsActive rising. An interactable with no timer has no such member, so its request is the start and both facts are published for one selection.
Interact_Timed.m_timerProgressRel, published on the fixed bands 0.1,0.2,...,1.0, at most once per band per interaction.

m_timerIsActive cleared while the shared counter stood below 1.0: the native abort path clears the member the trigger path clears too, so the counter is what tells the two apart. The reason carries the progress reached and, when the instance answers one, its refusal.
The interactor's own answer — `Interact_Base.IsBlocked` or the `PlayerCanInteract` the caller read — naming a request the game will not accept. The debug sentence is never read.

derived: `cancelled` is derived: the game assigns `OnInteractionEvaluationAbort` and `OnInteractionTriggered` per prefab, so the event that would name an abort directly is not always subscribed. The row is published from the timer window closing below the top of its range, which is the shared counter rather than a callback argument.

The `object` port is the map-object entity of the interactable when the map-object half addresses it (`door/*`, `terminal/*`). An interactable no map-object category addresses — a resource locker, a generator, a button — publishes without the port; see the note below.
`progressed` is quantised by this module and not by the game: the game publishes its own `TimerUpdated` every frame, which is not a fact stream.
notes: The interaction of a `gtfo.map_object` door is the door the map-object half addresses: `LG_SecurityDoor` is both. A terminal's interactable is `Interact_ComputerTerminal`, whose `m_terminal` is the `LG_ComputerTerminal` the address is built from, so the hook climbs through that field before asking the map-object lookup.

`Interact_Timed` is the base of most held interactions (`Interact_ComputerTerminal`, `Interact_Hack`, `Interact_ManualTimedWithCallback`, `Interact_Revive`, `Interact_SecurityDoorUseKeyItem`), so the timer readback covers all of them with one patch. The instant ones are `Interact_Base` subclasses and are covered by the selection readback.

The same patch serves `forge.trigger.player.revive_started` and `forge.trigger.player.revive_cancelled`: a revive is an `Interact_Timed`, so the window this module tracks is the one those rows need. They are a different slice's rows, so nothing here publishes them.
